title: diagram block props
description: A flow, a decision, a map of ideas, written in Mermaid and drawn when the course is built (by Pele): nodes appear by depth and edges draw; pointing at a node lights the path that leads to it.
x-ai-instructions: One chart says one thing: write takeaway as the finding, set highlight to the item that proves it, keep labels short (they are translated). On a narrated screen, give items an at anchor to the word that names them (see skill elabora-charts). Allowed: flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, mindmap, timeline, journey, ishikawa, venn. Write labels in the course language; no style, classDef or colours (the theme colours the diagram). Keep it under about 15 nodes.

takeaway.description: The sentence the chart proves, shown as its title: "Most incidents start with an email", not "Incidents by origin".

context.description: Only what neither the title nor the chart says (the unit, the population or the period the axes do not give), in one line under the title. Most charts need none; never a rephrasing of the takeaway.

source.description: Where the diagram comes from, shown under it.

mermaid.description: The diagram in Mermaid syntax, its words in the course language.

labels.description: Words of nodes and edges by id (as Pele names them: a flowchart node's id, an edge's L_<from>_<to>_<n>, a mind map node's words), replacing the Mermaid text's. Translations write here.

beats.description: Narrated screens: nodes brought by the voice.

node.description: The node's id in the source.

highlight.description: Id of the node that carries the idea (an outcome): it takes the accent colour.

spotlightEnd.description: Narrated screens: when the voice is done with the items, so they all stand again and the highlight takes the colour. Default: the end of the line where the last item came.

revealOnBeats.description: Narrated screens with item moments: each item appears at its moment (true), or every item is there from the start and the moments only move the spotlight (false).
